title: POC credits & benchmark sprint - AriaHealth kickoff
summary: Kickoff to scope a 4-week POC: define success criteria (latency, throughput, clinical accuracy), workload sizing for benchmarks, and commercial guardrails (pilot credits, trial terms, commercial path). Redwood AE+SE covered Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and proposed benchmark plan. Action items: share security pack, provide pilot credit quote, schedule benchmark window week of Dec 8.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. With me are Hannah, our SE, and Diego from solutions. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Jules: Jules here, Head of ML at AriaHealth. Priya and Evan also on.
[00:18] Priya: Hi all.
[00:20] Evan: Evan, Cloud Ops.
[00:22] Maya: Maya, legal—I'll jump in at procurement parts.
[00:26] Hannah: Great. Agenda for today is to agree scope for the proof of concept, clarify success criteria, and cover the commercial side—credits, length, procurement path.
[00:36] Samir: Quick context from our side: you mentioned a clinical summarization workload and a secure deployment requirement. Correct?
[00:42] Jules: Yeah, the main ask is ingesting de-identified consult notes and generating short summaries and suggested follow-ups. We need model outputs to match clinical accuracy thresholds and pass a basic hallucination audit. Latency target is sub-700ms p95 on 256 token responses for the main flow. Throughput varies—initially ~50 rps during peak test windows, average more like 10.
[01:04] Hannah: Okay, that maps to two benchmark modes: latency-focused single-request SLOs and throughput run for sustained concurrency. We'll plan for a small latency bench and a 30-minute sustained throughput window.
[01:14] Evan: On infra we prefer V P C/private deployment or at least VPC peering—PHI controls. Is Redwood Private an option for a pilot?
[01:22] Diego: You can do Redwood Private in customer V P C but initial pilots often run on dedicated instances with strict network controls. For procurement speed we sometimes start hosted with a dedicated pool and then transition to private for the production step.
[01:35] Priya: What's the difference on cost and latency between hosted dedicated and Private on prem?
[01:40] Hannah: Hosted dedicated gives fastest time to start—Redwood spins up reserved GPU pools for your tenant. Latency differences are minimal; Private adds networking overhead if on-prem or through a managed V P C, but gives stronger control and K M S integrations. Costwise Private has platform licensing and potentially infra carry. We'll surface estimates in the credits quote.
[01:59] Jules: Sounds fair. For the POC we want the simplest path that still satisfies compliance so we can iterate quickly.
[02:06] Samir: Commercial guardrails—our standard pilot playbook for an enterprise POC is 4 weeks, with an optional 2-week extension. We provide a pool of pilot credits that cover compute for benchmark runs and initial integration. Typically that is quoted as a credit slab with an expiration date.
[02:23] Maya: Legal preference is a short-term MSA addendum plus an SOW. We need audit logs and data retention policies up front.
[02:31] Samir: We'll send the security pack and a one-page pilot SOW template.
[02:34] Jules: On success criteria—aside from latency and throughput, we need clinical accuracy at least 92% on our rubric, and hallucination rate under 3% as measured on our dev set. Also integration viability with our existing queueing and K V cache patterns.
[02:51] Hannah: We'll build the bench harness to run your dev set and the two modes. We'll capture token-level latency, p50/p95/p99, and failure rates. For hallucination metrics we'll run your golden prompts and compare against ground truth; note that automatic scoring might need manual adjudication for edge cases.
[03:09] Evan: For workload sizing—50 rps peak with 256 token output. What kind of GPU footprint should we expect for the throughput run?
[03:16] Hannah: Rough estimate: for a 7B-13B parameter class open model, you'll need 1-2 A100-equivalent GPUs per 50 rps depending on batching and KV cache usage. If you go quantized 4-bit variants, footprint drops. But for clinical accuracy you may want the 13B float/quant hybrid. We'll propose a suggested config in the benchmark plan.
[03:38] Jules: We also want a steady-state cost estimate. Can Redwood give a cost-per-1k-token at the config you propose?
[03:44] Samir: Yes — part of the deliverable is an econ slide: cost per 1k tokens across the candidate model configs and with/without KV caching. We'll include cache hit assumptions you provide.
[03:55] Maya: On data retention and K M S—does Redwood's hosted option allow customer-managed keys?
[04:00] Diego: Hosted can integrate with customer K M S via our enterprise package; Private obviously supports customer K M S and H S M integrations. We'll include our K M S integration doc.
[04:09] Priya: Timeline—if we sign the pilot SOW by Dec 5, when can bench runs start?
[04:14] Samir: We can schedule bench provisioning the week of Dec 8. Two weeks of integration/ingest, then one week of benchmarks, then a final wrap review week. So final review around Jan 9. That's the four-week cadence with slack.
[04:29] Jules: That works.
[04:31] Hannah: Bench plan details: 1) smoke test with 1000 records, 2) latency sweep across seq lengths, 3) 30-minute sustained concurrency at target rps, 4) hallucination/regression checks on dev set. We'll produce a results spreadsheet and recommender on model/quantization.
[04:53] Evan: For the 30-min sustained run—do you simulate prefix/K V cache distribution? Our real workload has many short prefixes which impact cache hit rates.
[05:01] Hannah: Good call. We'll run two throughput profiles: with warm KV cache (simulate high cache hit) and a cold-start profile that measures regen overhead. We'll need a sample of your prefix distribution.
[05:13] Jules: We'll provide a 10k-record sample of consults and a prefix frequency histogram.
[05:18] Samir: Commercial credits—typical Redwood pilot credit structure: we allocate a compute credit pool that covers X GPU-hours mapped to the proposed config. Unused credits expire after 90 days. For this POC we propose a 3000-credit slab which roughly maps to the planned bench plus some integration buffer; exact mapping and price will be in the quote.
[05:37] Priya: Is there a way to convert credits to committed usage if we go to Dedicated?
[05:42] Diego: Yes, credits can be applied toward a first-term committed contract or consumed as pre-paid usage; we'll outline conversion mechanics.
[05:49] Maya: For procurement path—short SOW for pilot, then if successful we expect a procurement RFx for Dedicated capacity and an enterprise MSA. We need to know estimated lead times and any long-term SLAs.
[06:01] Samir: Lead time for Dedicated pools is ~2-4 weeks post-contract depending on region. SLAs are part of the Dedicated package and we'll share the SLA doc in the security pack.
[06:11] Jules: Bench success gates—can we set an objective pass/fail matrix? E.g., p95 < 700ms, clinical F1 >= 0.92, hallucination < 3%, errors < 0.5% during throughput run.
[06:24] Hannah: Absolutely, we'll include the pass/fail criteria in the SOW. Note that hallucination measurement sometimes needs manual review—we can run a small adjudication batch if needed.
[06:34] Evan: On metrics telemetry—do you provide token-level tracing and per-request ids we can tie back to our logs?
[06:40] Diego: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns for the pilot. For Private deployments we can forward logs to your SIEM or S3.
[06:52] Jules: Any blockers you foresee?
[06:54] Hannah: The main blocker is access to a representative prefix distribution and dev set for hallucination scoring. Also legal needs the security pack and a short MSA. From our side we need an agreed pilot SOW and the credit acceptance.
[07:08] Maya: We'll review the security pack but need data processing terms in the SOW.
[07:12] Samir: Noted, we'll include a DPA appendix.
[07:15] Jules: Regarding models—do you curate a model catalog or do we bring our own fine-tuned model?
[07:20] Hannah: Both. We have a Redwood-verified model catalog with recommended quantizations; you can also bring a fine-tuned checkpoint. For the POC it's often easiest to test with a validated open model, then iterate with your fine-tuned model in the bench.
[07:33] Priya: Suppose we need a private deployment for compliance—does that change pilot credit structure?
[07:38] Samir: It can. Private often requires a flat platform fee plus compute consumption; for pilots we can structure credits to cover compute and waive initial platform fees in some cases. We'll mark that as a conditional in the quote.
[07:51] Evan: Scheduling—can we lock Dec 9-11 for integration and Dec 15 for the long throughput run?
[07:58] Samir: We'll tentatively reserve those dates, pending SOW sign.
[08:02] Jules: On success criteria measurement—how do you handle differences between automated scoring and clinician review?
[08:08] Hannah: We'll run automatic scoring and then a clinician adjudication sample of ~200 cases to validate. The final pass/fail on hallucination will take into account the adjudication.
[08:19] Maya: Financial approvals—who signs off on credits? Our procurement needs the credit amount and expiry in the SOW.
[08:25] Samir: We'll provide a one-line credit table in the SOW and a separate pricing worksheet.
[08:29] Diego: Also, competitor mention: if you want vendor neutrality, we can propose multi-model candidate baseline (Anthro-, OpenAI-ish, or open models) to show delta.
[08:39] Jules: We may baseline against Anthropic and an internal LLM.
[08:43] Samir: Good, we'll include competitor columns in the bench spreadsheet.
[08:47] Priya: Any security red flags for PHI?
[08:50] Diego: None we expect to be deal-stoppers; just need approved DPA, K M S integration, and a network plan for V P C if Private. We'll include SOC2 attestation and penetration test reports.
[09:01] Samir: Ok let's recap and next steps.
[09:04] Samir: Redwood will: 1) send security pack and pilot SOW template by EOD Nov 28, 2) provide a detailed quote with proposed credit slab and model configs by Dec 3, 3) reserve tentative bench window Dec 9–15, 4) prepare bench harness and request sample data (10k records + prefix histogram).
[09:24] Jules: AriaHealth will: 1) share the 10k sample and prefix distribution by Dec 2, 2) legal will review pilot SOW and DPA, 3) procurement to review credit slab and sign by Dec 5 if approved.
[09:36] Maya: We'll try to turn legal in 3 business days.
[09:39] Evan: I'll coordinate network and infra contacts for the V P C plan.
[09:42] Samir: Great. Final Qs?
[09:44] Priya: No more from me.
[09:45] Jules: Good.
[09:46] Samir: Thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the pack and the quote.
[09:49] Hannah: I'll own the bench run plan and be point for technical questions—email hannah@redwood.ai.
[09:56] Diego: And I'll coordinate legal/commercial items.
[10:00] Maya: Thanks all.
[10:02] Samir: Meeting adjourned.
